name: Bajadasaurus
sum: Bajadasaurus is a dicraeosaurid sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Patagonia known from a skull and neck with elongated spines.
wsnote: The cited text compares dicraeosaurids with Asian elephants but gives no length for this genus.
holotype: A single specimen found in 2010, including a largely complete skull and parts of the neck; the number was not read. Bone fusion shows the individual was adult.
material: Skull and neck vertebrae from the Bajada Colorada Formation, Argentina; the skull is crushed.
biology: Its very long neural spines have been discussed as part of a defence system; its skull and neck were later restudied in detail.
author: Gallina et al. 2019
